- Certified type: Water meter intended for metering of cold potable water and hot water. Rotary piston meter (OCR says "Roating piston" - likely "Rotating piston") with mechanical indicating device 8R MD or 7R MD. Type: RTKD

- Date issued: 29.04.2016 (from signatures). Page 1 doesn't have an explicit date issue... The signature date 29.04.2016 appears. Let's use that as date_issued.

- Recommendation: R49, edition 2013, with parts 1, 2, 3. The certificate references R49-1 (2013), R49-2 (2013), R49-3 (2013). The canonical id should be "R49". Edition: 2013. Accuracy classes: for water meters, accuracy class 2 (±2%)... Actually the accuracy class in the table: ±2% for water temp ≤30°C, ±3% for >30°C, ±5% for Q1≤Q≤Q2. Hmm. R49 water meters have accuracy classes 1 and 2. The values here are maximum permissible errors, not class per se. The class is 2 (since ±2% in upper zone for cold water). But the table shows MAP values. I'll record accuracy_classes as ["2"]? Actually R49 water meter accuracy classes are 1 and 2. Given ±2% upper zone, it's class 2. But temperature >30°C gives ±3%. Hmm, per R49-1:2013, for class 2: ±5% in lower zone (Q1≤Q≤Q2), ±2% in upper zone for water temperature within temperature class... Actually for hot water, MPE differs. Let me record the characteristics as config_level or just type_level strings.

- RTKD Q3-10 8R MD dated 29.04.2016, 45 pages

Page total: 3 pages ("Page 1 of 3 pages").

Scheme: The certificate number R49/2013-DE1-16.03 — scheme isn't explicitly stated. OIML-CS has scheme A and B. This 2016 cert predates formal scheme labeling; PTB basic certificate. I'll omit scheme or set null. The instructions say scheme (A|B). Not present — omit.

Model family: The type RTKD comes in variants. Looking at the type details table:

Columns: Q3 (m³/h): 6,3 and 10 — two columns corresponding to the two model variants. Q4: 7,87 and 12,5. Q2/Q1: 1.6 (both). Body length: ≥260 mm (both). Nominal diameter: ≥25 (col 1), ≥32 (col 2). Q2 any orientation: col1: 0,252/0,2/0,16/0,126/0,1/0,08/0,063/0,05; col2: 0,4/0,32/0,254/0,2/0,16/0,128/0,1/0,08/0,064/0,051. Q3/Q1: col1: 40/50/63/80/100/125/160/200; col2: 40/50/63/80/100/125/160/200/250/315. Pressure loss class: ΔP40 (col1), ΔP63 (col2). Minimum scale interval: 0.02 l (both).

Temperature class: T30/T50 (both).

Accuracy class: ±2% (Q2≤Q≤Q4) for water temp ≤30°C; ±3% (Q2≤Q≤Q4) for water temp >30°C; ±5% (Q1≤Q≤Q2).

Pressure range: 0.3 bar to 16 bar ("0.3 bar bis 16 bar" - German "bis" = to).

Minimum straight length of inlet/outlet pipe: 0mm/0mm.

Climatic environment: 5°C to 55°C.

So there are two model variants distinguished by Q3: 6.3 and 10. Model IDs: "RTKD Q3=6.3" and "RTKD Q3=10". The test reports mention "RTKD Q3-6,3 7R MD" and "RTKD Q3-10 8R MD", plus "RTKD-S Q3-4 190 MOD" (a third variant? RTKD-S with Q3=4). Hmm, the RTKD-S Q3-4 190 MOD has a test report but the type details table only shows two columns (6.3 and 10). The type designation says "8R MD or 7R MD" indicating devices. RTKD-S seems a special variant. Should I include it in model family? The type details table only covers RTKD. The test report mentions RTKD-S Q3-4 190 MOD. I think models should be based on the type details: two variants Q3=6.3 and Q3=10. But the cert also covers RTKD-S... Hmm.

Actually, the certified type identification: "Rotating piston meter with mechanical indicating device 8R MD or 7R MD. Type: RTKD". The test reports include RTKD-S Q3-4 190 MOD — 190 MOD might be register type. The type details page says "Type details RTKD" and shows two columns. I'll create model family with two models based on Q3: 6.3 and 10. But the RTKD-S variant... I could mention it in type_designations or in description. Let me think about model naming. The test report IDs give clean model names: "RTKD Q3-6,3 7R MD" and "RTKD Q3-10 8R MD". I could use those as model_ids but normalized: "RTKD Q3=6.3 (7R MD)" and "RTKD Q3=10 (8R MD)".

Hmm, but the "7R MD" vs "8R MD" — indicating device types. And RTKD-S Q3-4 190 MOD is a third model with a test report. Since the type details table doesn't include it, I'll include the two from the table, and maybe add RTKD-S as a third model with the info from test report only? Risky to fabricate. Better: models per test report names since those are the certified configurations: 
- RTKD Q3-6,3 7R MD
- RTKD Q3-10 8R MD
- RTKD-S Q3-4 190 MOD

And the type details table gives attributes for two of them (Q3=6.3 and Q3=10). I could map values to models "Q3=6.3" and "Q3=10". 

Let me structure model_level characteristics with models "RTKD Q3=6.3" and "RTKD Q3=10". Actually the instructions in the R137 example used the size as model_id (e.g., "G2.5"). Here the equivalent distinguishing parameter is Q3. But actual model designations from test reports: "RTKD Q3-6,3 7R MD". I'll use these full designations as model_ids since they're explicit, but the table only distinguishes by Q3. Hmm, simpler: model_id "RTKD Q3-6,3 7R MD" → normalized "RTKD Q3-6.3 7R MD". And "RTKD Q3-10 8R MD". For RTKD-S Q3-4 190 MOD, no type details given. I could include it in models list but with no attribute values. That might be fine — it's covered by the certificate (has a test report). Let me include all three models, and in model_level characteristics only provide values for the two that have data. Actually, would that be misleading? The matrix table would then have rows only for two models. That's fine.

Wait — reconsider: is RTKD-S a separate type or a variant? "RTKD-S Q3-4 190 MOD" — 85 pages test report. The certificate identifies type RTKD; RTKD-S might be a special version. Given the uncertainty, including it in models with the note is reasonable. Alternatively keep model_family with two models matching the type table and mention RTKD-S in type_designations/description. Hmm.

The schema says model_family: include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. The cert covers multiple variants. I'll include three models:
- {"model_id": "RTKD Q3-6.3 7R MD", "label": "Q3 = 6.3 m³/h, mechanical indicating device 7R MD"}
- {"model_id": "RTKD Q3-10 8R MD", "label": "Q3 = 10 m³/h, mechanical indicating device 8R MD"}
- {"model_id": "RTKD-S Q3-4 190 MOD", "label": "Q3 = 4, register 190 MOD"}

Hmm, the labels add info from test report names — that's fine, it's derived.

Now the matrix table: extract the type details table.

matrix_tables:
- name: "Type details RTKD"
- columns: ["q3", "q4", "q2_q1_ratio", "body_length", "nominal_diameter", "connection_type", "q1_any_orientation", "q2_any_orientation", "q3_q1_ratio", "pressure_loss_class", "minimum_scale_interval", ...]

Hmm, the table is transposed: rows are attributes, columns are the two model variants. The schema for matrix_tables has columns[] and rows[] (object per row). I could restructure so each row is a model: rows: [{"model": "RTKD Q3-6.3 7R MD", "q3": 6.3, "q4": 7.87, ...}, {...}]. That fits better. Columns: ["model", "q3", "q4", "q2_q1_ratio", "body_length", "nominal_diameter", "connection_type", "q1_any_orientation", "q2_any_orientation", "q3_q1_ratio", "pressure_loss_class", "minimum_scale_interval"]. Column units where applicable.

But the multi-valued lists (Q1 values, Q2 values, Q3/Q1 ratios) are lists per model. In matrix_tables rows, I could store them as arrays or as strings. The schema example shows numeric values in rows. I'll store lists as arrays of numbers for Q1, Q2, and Q3/Q1 ratios.

Also the second table (temperature class, accuracy class, pressure range, environmental class, etc.) applies to both models (colspan=2). Those go in type_level characteristics.

Let me now build the characteristics.

type_level (whole-cert attributes):
- temperature_class: value "T30 / T50" — it's a list of two classes. Value as string "T30/T50"? Or list. I'll do value: "T30/T50" as a string. Or maybe better as list ["T30","T50"]. Schema says value: number | {min,max} | string. So string "T30/T50".
- maximum_permitted_error_upper_zone_cold: ±2% (Q2≤Q≤Q4) for water temp ≤30°C. This is config-level: axis = water temperature. Actually accuracy class entries:
  - ±2 % for Q2≤Q≤Q4, water temperature ≤30°C
  - ±3 % for Q2≤Q≤Q4, water temperature >30°C
  - ±5 % for Q1≤Q≤Q2
  These could be config_level entries: attribute "maximum_permitted_error", axis "flow_zone_and_water_temperature", values with conditions.
  
  config_level:
  - attribute: "maximum_permitted_error", axis: "flow range / water temperature"
    - {condition: "Q2 ≤ Q ≤ Q4, water temperature ≤ 30 °C", value: 2, unit_symbol: "%"}
    - {condition: "Q2 ≤ Q ≤ Q4, water temperature > 30 °C", value: 3, unit_symbol: "%"}
    - {condition: "Q1 ≤ Q ≤ Q2", value: 5, unit_symbol: "%"}

  Note "für" is German "for".
  
- pressure_range: {min: 0.3, max: 16}, unit: "bar"

- minimum_straight_length_inlet_outlet_pipe: 0mm/0mm → could be two attributes: minimum_straight_length_inlet_pipe: 0 mm; minimum_straight_length_outlet_pipe: 0 mm. Or one: value "0 mm / 0 mm". I'll split into two for cleanliness. Actually the instruction about splitting (voltage/frequency) suggests splitting. I'll do:

  - minimum_straight_length_outlet_pipe: value 0, unit mm

model_level:
- q3 (nominal flow rate): values: {"model": "RTKD Q3-6.3 7R MD", value: 6.3, unit m³/h}, {"model": "RTKD Q3-10 8R MD", value: 10}

The rule says lists of values represent model matrix... but here it's a list of possible Q1 values for one model (different metrological configurations: Q3/Q1 ratios 40...200 correspond to different Q1 settings). Indeed Q1 = Q3/ratio: 6.3/40 = 0.1575 ≈ 0.157; 6.3/50=0.126; 6.3/63≈0.1; 6.3/80=0.0788≈0.078; 6.3/100=0.063; 6.3/125=0.0504≈0.050; 6.3/160≈0.039≈0.040; 6.3/200=0.0315≈0.032.   Best representation: config_level with axis "Q3/Q1 ratio":
  - attribute: "minimum_flow_rate_q1", axis: "q3_q1_ratio", values: [{condition: "40", value: 0.157}, {condition: "50", value: 0.126}, ...] — but this is per model. The config values don't have a model field per schema: values[]: {condition, value}. Hmm, config_level entries are attribute × config-axis matrix. But here we have model × config. The schema example for config_level (rule 5): "2-sensor-row vs 4-sensor-row setups". Values follow {condition, value, unit_symbol}.

  Option: create two config_level entries, one per model:
  - attribute: "minimum_flow_rate_q1", axis: "Q3/Q1 ratio (model RTKD Q3-6.3 7R MD)", values: [{condition: "40", value: 0.157}, ...]
  - attribute: "minimum_flow_rate_q1", axis: "Q3/Q1 ratio (model RTKD Q3-10 8R MD)", values: [{condition: "40", value: 0.25}, ...]

  Similarly q2: Q2 = 1.6 × Q1: 0.157×1.6 = 0.2512 ≈ 0.252 ✓. So:
  - attribute: "transitional_flow_rate_q2", axis: "Q3/Q1 ratio (model ...)", values pairing with Q1 list.

  And attribute "q3_q1_ratio" could be model_level with lists: value as list [40,50,...]. Schema value types: number | {min,max} | string. A list isn't allowed as value. I could represent as string "40/50/63/80/100/125/160/200". That's reasonable. Or put the ratio list in the axis conditions (already there). I'll add model_level: "q3_q1_ratio" with string values of the slash-separated list. Hmm, that duplicates. Let me include it as string for completeness: {"model": "RTKD Q3-6.3 7R MD", "value": "40/50/63/80/100/125/160/200"}. Acceptable.

- pressure_loss_class: "ΔP 40" (model 1), "ΔP 63" (model 2). Unit "bar". Value: 40 and 63, unit bar? The class designation ΔP40 corresponds to max pressure loss 0.4 bar? Actually in R49, pressure loss classes: Δp40 = 0.4 bar (0.04 MPa? no). R49-1:2013 pressure-loss classes: Δp10..Δp63 where Δp63 = 0.63 bar? Hmm: classes are Δp10, Δp16, Δp25, Δp40, Δp63 with max pressure loss in bar equal to class/100. ΔP40 → 0.4 bar. So value 40, unit_symbol "bar"? That would be wrong (0.4 bar). Better: value string "ΔP 40" with unit null, or value 40 with unit_symbol null and attribute pressure_loss_class. I'll use value: "ΔP 40" string, unit null. Safe.
